sentence_audit.sentence: Prespecified subgroups were defined by sex, age, AMI subtype, primary AMI position, admission urgency and initial care unit.
Discrimination was evaluated using the locked out-of-fold predictions.
High-need calibration used the binary target y>=3.
For each subgroup, we fitted a logistic calibration model on logit probabilities.
Patient-level bootstrap resampling produced 95% confidence intervals for slope, intercept and Brier score.
Subgroups were not refitted separately.
Estimates required at least 30 patients, 10 events and 10 non-events.
All 16 prespecified scenarios are reported in Table 16 and Figure 7B.
Each estimate remains on its original outcome scale.
Deltas are shown only when the outcome scale is unchanged.
The 6-hour and 72-hour landmark cohorts had lower macro-AUC than the 24-hour cohort.
Estimates were 0.761 (delta -0.0173) and 0.751 (delta -0.0269), respectively.
Primary-position AMI increased macro-AUC by 0.0140, whereas excluding type 2 MI increased it by 0.0066.
Multiple imputation, troponin exclusion, treatment adjustment and against-advice exclusion changed estimates by at most 0.0009.
The reversed-direction, time-permuted and generic-smoothness controls remained within 0.006 of their references.
No scenario replaced the primary analysis after inspection.
Table 17 reports subgroup discrimination, high-need calibration slopes and Brier scores.
Fourteen prespecified subgroup strata were estimable.
XGB-static+TS point estimates ranged from 0.729 in patients aged 80 years or older to 0.812 in STEMI.
DG-GRU+TR ranged from 0.664 to 0.784.
DG-GRU+TR minus XGB-static+TS was negative in every subgroup.
The confidence interval crossed zero only for Other or unspecified MI (n=193).
Overall high-need calibration was better for XGB-static+TS than for DG-GRU+TR.
The calibration slopes were 1.188 (1.128 to 1.253) and 0.638 (0.598 to 0.680), respectively.
XGB-static+TS slopes exceeded 1 in every estimable stratum, indicating under-confident probabilities.
DG-GRU+TR slopes were below 1 in every estimable stratum, indicating over-confident probabilities.
The largest DG-GRU+TR miscalibrations occurred for age >=80 (slope 0.494; intercept 0.450) and type 2 MI (slope 0.504).
Calibration was closest to 1 in CCU/CVICU (DG-GRU+TR slope 0.983).
These patterns do not change the discrimination ranking.
In CCU/CVICU, DG-GRU+TR had a near-ideal slope but lower macro-AUC than XGB-static+TS (0.721 vs 0.773).
Subgroup estimates are descriptive because models were not refitted within strata.
Table 17.
Prespecified subgroup discrimination and high-need calibration.
High need denotes outcome level 3 or higher.
AUC denotes five-class macro-AUC.
Slopes and Brier scores used locked out-of-fold predictions.
The 2-patient non-emergency stratum was not estimable.
The six-level outcome produced macro-AUC 0.776 on its own scale.
Merged disposition labels produced 0.800 on a different four-class scale.
These values neither replace nor directly subtract from the primary five-level estimate.
Primary-position restriction and type 2 MI exclusion increased the five-level estimate by 0.0140 and 0.0066, respectively.
In eICU, excluding the Other disposition category increased DG-GRU+TR macro-AUC from 0.729 to 0.735.
Patient-safe hospital-cluster bootstrap gave 0.729 (0.714 to 0.744).
The hospital-cluster interval is wider than the patient-grouped interval.
The primary direction remained unchanged.
None of these analyses replaced the prespecified primary estimand.
They quantify sensitivity to outcome definition and evaluation unit, not a new primary comparison.
Absolute discrimination therefore depends on outcome granularity, cohort restriction and clustering.
Calibration varied by database and subgroup, so local recalibration remains necessary.
Subgroup analysis extends this calibration evidence.
XGB-static+TS discriminated better across estimable strata, but calibration slopes varied.
DG-GRU+TR was well calibrated in CCU/CVICU but remained less discriminative.
Subgroup-specific recalibration therefore requires prospective evaluation rather than assuming transportability.
Subgroup analyses reused locked out-of-fold predictions and were descriptive.
They did not estimate subgroup-specific treatment effects or refit models within strata.
Figure 7.
Prespecified subgroup contrasts and all 16 sensitivity analyses.
(a) Paired subgroup contrasts for DG-GRU+TR minus XGB-static+TS; negative values indicate lower DG-GRU+TR macro-AUC.
(b) Sensitivity estimates; six-level and merged-label scenarios use separate scales and omit deltas.
Negative values are retained.
